Title: Sleeping Mind restored to its former glory?

Messages.Author: Brian
Messages.Body:
If the allies who can use cards requiring a discipline "as a vampire"
are treated as a vampire only by the card, then should a vampire who
can block "as if untapped" be treated as untapped only for purposes of
blocking?

Basically, just because Wake with Evening's Freshness and Forced
Awakening allow you to "block" as though untapped, that wouldn't mean
they let you "avoid Sleeping Mind" as though untapped. Sleeping Mind
wouldn't register Spiridonas using WWEF as untapped, any more than it
would see Ghouled Street Thug using IG as a vampire.

I don't think Dominate needs yet another awesome card, I just think
that this follows from the same reasoning as the Ally thing.

--Brian

Messages.Author: Brian
Messages.Body:
> Sorry, doesn't follow at all. Wake lets you "block and play reactions" as
> though untapped. Sleeping Mind says you can't block if you are tapped.

There is, to my knowledge, no rule prohibiting a vampire from being
tapped and being regarded as untapped simultaneously.

If Sleeping Mind prohibited all vampires <except untapped ones> from
blocking, then a vampire considered untapped could block (even if
tapped).

However, it prohibits all vampires <which are tapped> from blocking,
so I think a tapped vampire cannot block (even if also considered
untapped).

It makes _no sense_ that a vampire can be both untapped and tapped,
but hey, it also makes no sense that an ally can go to torpor. Once
again, there is no rule prohibiting simultaneous tapped and untapped
status.

Or is there? LSJ?

--Brian

But it's not a tapped vampire doing the blocking; it's an untapped
vampire. Or, specifically, it's a vampire who is considered untapped
for purposes of blocking and playing reaction cards, per card text.

No tapped vampire can ever block, is the problem. Only untapped
vampires can block. Sleeping Mind's original card text was FUBAR.

>It makes _no sense_ that a vampire can be both untapped and tapped,
>but hey, it also makes no sense that an ally can go to torpor. Once
>again, there is no rule prohibiting simultaneous tapped and untapped
>status.
>

There's no rule prohibiting it, but there's a physical problem; the card
is either upwise or sideways. You can't be both tapped and untapped at
the same time.

You can, however, be tapped and be able to play some cards AS IF you
were untapped, much like allies are able to play some cards AS IF they
were a vampire.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:


There is a standing, no-card-needed, rule that says only untapped
minions can block. This is equivalent in every respect to saying
that tapped minions cannot block.

Wake overcomes that restriction. It doesn't make the vampire be both
untapped and tapped.

Sleeping Mind, in it's original printing, restated that basic
restriction from the basic rules.

Wake overcomes that restriction. It doesn't make the vampire be both
untapped and tapped.

To rule that wkae didn't overcome the restriction would be to rule
that Wake has no effect.

Messages.Author: LSJ
Messages.Body:
Henrik Isaksson wrote:
> How do you think that the designers would have worded the original sleeping
> mind if they had the intent that it would in fact counter wake? (i.e. that a
> minion playing wake couldn't block)

They obviously had that intent in mind, of course.
And they ended up writing the card in a way that failed to achieve that effect.

The courses of action at that time were to let card text stand or to issue
errata for the sake of "designer intent". Issuing errata to match designer
intent would also have increaed the power of the card. So while designer
intent is one of the criteria for issuing errata, balance is weighed
even more heavily. Result: no errata issued (and thus the card plays by
it's weaker actual text instead of the stronger designer intent).

To achieve the effect they wanted, they could've used something like:
"Choose all tapped minions. The chosen minions cannot block." (together
with the rest of the card's effect - which they probably would've
dropped if they had used that wording - that is they would've likely
gone with "As above, but choose all tapped minions." and allowed the
tapped minions to untap via Rat's Warning or whatnot).

Messages.Author: Brian
Messages.Body:
> > It makes _no sense_ that a vampire can be both untapped and tapped,
> > but hey, it also makes no sense that an ally can go to torpor. Once
> > again, there is no rule prohibiting simultaneous tapped and untapped
> > status.
> >
> > Or is there? LSJ?
>
> There is a standing, no-card-needed, rule that says only untapped
> minions can block. This is equivalent in every respect to saying
> that tapped minions cannot block.

Only if being considered untapped means you are not considered tapped.

Most players assume this is the case, but I have found nowhere in the
rules stating a minion cannot be simultaneously considered tapped and
untapped.

If, on the other hand, "untapped" and "tapped" are only /USUALLY/
mutally exclusive by game state, but can be acheived simultaneously by
card play, then the two statements do not amount to the same thing.

> Wake overcomes that restriction. It doesn't make the vampire be both
> untapped and tapped.

The vampire is tapped (game state). The vampire is untapped (card
text). As there is no mention that it ceases to be either, it remains
both.

> Sleeping Mind, in it's original printing, restated that basic
> restriction from the basic rules.

Sleeping Mind said tapped vampires could not block, as opposed to only
untapped vampires could.

> Wake overcomes that restriction. It doesn't make the vampire be both
> untapped and tapped.

If that's a ruling, of course, you win. In fact, I WANT "untapped" to
preclude "tapped", for common sense reasons. Still, listen to the
rest, below.

> To rule that wkae didn't overcome the restriction would be to rule
> that Wake has no effect.

Only untapped vampires may block.
If this vampire is both tapped and untapped, then this vampire may
block.

Tapped vampires may not block.
If this vampire is both tapped and untapped, then this vampire may not
block.

Do you see the difference between these two?
This is why "tapped vampires may not block" is different from "only
untapped vampires may block". If I'm correct, this means the old text
for sleeping mind has meaning (without disturbing any other card's
functionality).
